text:
I rode the elevator to the eleventh floor, and as I got out, the operator said "Have a good day, son"
"Don't call me son," I said. "You're not my dad."
He scratched his head. "No, but I brought you up, didn't I?"
gist: Elevator operator calls a passenger son and defends it by saying he brought him up, meaning carried him upstairs.

wordplay.explanation: 'brought you up' means raised you as a child and took you up in the elevator.

characters.looks: grown man in suit, annoyed
old man in bellhop uniform and cap

text:
My best friend passed away recently, and grieving before his grave I said,
"Bro, I really miss you. My wife has been pregnant for 8 months now. How about you reincarnate as my child?"
A month later, my wife gave birth to a big boy. As my child grew older each day, I realized he looks a lot like my best friend.
I'm really happy that my prayer worked.
gist: A man asks his dead best friend to reincarnate as his unborn son, and takes the boy's resemblance to the friend as proof the prayer worked, missing the affair.

characters.looks: naive happy man, flowers, black suit
pregnant woman, nervous sideways glance
boy who looks exactly like the dead friend
best friend in photo on gravestone, distinctive mustache

text:
A young artist exhibits his work for the first time...
.. and a well known art critic is in attendance.
The critic says to the young artist, "would you like my opinion on your work?"
"Yes, " says the artist.
"It's worthless," says the critic
The artist replies, "I know, but tell me anyway."
gist: A critic offers a young artist his opinion, calls the work worthless, and the artist replies he knows but wants to hear it anyway, mistaking the verdict for the opinion's value.

characters.looks: young artist, beret, paint-stained smock, hopeful
snooty older man, scarf, monocle, glass of wine

text:
Little Johnny was told by his friends that adults have a deep dark secret and can be easily manipulated.
Johnny decides to test it. He comes home, goes up to his mother and says, "Mom, I know everything." Mom shushes him and gives him $10.
"Just don't tell Dad" she says.
*Hey, it's working* thinks Little Johnny.
An hour later, Dad comes home from work. Johnny goes up to him and says: "Dad, I know everything."
Dad gives Johnny $100. "Don't tell Mom" he says.
Just then, the mailman knocks on the door. Johnny opens it and says. "I know everything, Mister."
The mailman drops all his mail, his eyes tear up  and he says:
"Well then Johnny, come give Daddy a hug."
gist: A boy tells each adult 'I know everything' and collects hush money from mom and dad, until the mailman reveals he is the boy's real father.

characters.looks: freckled boy, cap, sly grin
nervous woman in apron, holding cash
man in office suit, briefcase, guilty look
mailman in uniform, mail bag, teary eyes

text: When I turned 16, my dad told me it was time to get a job. “When I was your age, my very first job I had I worked with over 500 people under me.”... “Wow!” I said. “Was it some big corporation?”“No.” He replied, “I mowed the lawn in the cemetery.”
gist: A father boasts that his first job had 500 people under him, which turns out to mean mowing a cemetery lawn.

wordplay.explanation: 'people under me' means subordinates and literally buried beneath him.

16-year-old boy, impressed wide eyes

At a wedding I whispered to a guy next to me,
"Isn't the bride a right ugly dog"
"Do you mind. That's my daughter you're talking about"
"I'm sorry, I didn't know you were her father''...
"I'm not . . . I'm her fucking mother.
